newsitem.title: USA: House calls on China to honor Hong Kong accord.
newsitem.headline: House calls on China to honor Hong Kong accord.

text.p: The U.S. House of Representatives on Tuesday approved a bill calling on China to honor its treaty obligations on Hong Kong, which reverts to Chinese rule on July 1.

The bill, approved by a 416-1 vote, declared that failure to have en elected legislature on Hong Kong would be a violation of the 1984 joint declaration with Britain and "calls on the Government of the People's Republic of China to honor its treaty obligations."

The measure stated that a free press and access to information "are fundamentally important" to Hong Kong's economic and commercial success and called on the Beijing government "to fully respect these essential rights."

The bill also called on the Beijing-appointed preparatory committee to reconsider its decision to amend the bill of rights ordinances and on the Chinese government to fully respect the autonomy and independence of the chief executive, civil service, judiciary, Hong Kong police and the Independent Commission against Corruption.
It set out factors the president must consider in determining whether Hong Kong is sufficiently autonomous following the Chinese takeover to justify treatment separate from mainland China.
These included continued cooperation from Hong Kong government agencies and preservation of the rule of law.
